Privacy

Last updated: 21 October 2026

The short version. Your chats, photos and memory notes are only visible to your account. When imy writes a reply, the recent messages and any photo you share are sent to our AI provider (Groq) to produce it, and screenshots you upload are sent to Groq to read the messages in them. Apart from the few services that run imy (listed below), we don't share them with anyone, and deleting your account removes them from imy. imy is for people aged 18 and over.

Who runs imy

imy is run by PDYN Technologies in the Philippines. You can reach us at the address under "Getting in touch" at the bottom of this page.

What imy stores

When you use imy, this is kept by imy. The database is hosted by Turso and uploaded pictures by Supabase (see "Who can see it"):

  • Your account: your email address and a scrambled version of your password. The password itself is never stored, so nobody — including whoever runs imy — can read it.
  • The people you set up: the name and nickname you give them, your answers to the interview questions, and the profile pictures you choose.
  • What you upload: the screenshots and the parts of chat exports you chose, and the messages imy reads out of them, with private details hidden (see the next section). Screenshot pictures are kept so imy can read them again if it gets better at it.
  • Your conversations in imy: what you send, what the person replies, reactions, and the photos and files you share in a chat.
  • Short notes imy keeps from your conversations — things like a date you mentioned — so replies can refer back to them. You can read and clear these in the chat menu.
  • One cookie that keeps you signed in. That's the only cookie. There is no advertising and no tracking across other websites. The pages don't load anything from another company either — no outside fonts, scripts or analytics — so opening imy tells nobody but imy that you did.
  • When your account was last active, and which days you used imy — so the people running it know how many people use it. Just dates, never what you did. Days older than about 13 months are deleted.
  • Visitor counts, without cookies: when you open the homepage or the app, imy counts the visit as a number for that day. To count each person once a day, it makes a code from your internet address, your browser's name and a secret that changes every day. The codes and the day's secret are deleted the next day, so visits can't be linked from one day to the next or traced back to you. If your browser sends "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control", you aren't counted at all.
  • Your time zone (like Asia/Manila), as your browser reports it, with that count and on your account. It's the only hint of where you are: the people running imy see a map with one dot per time zone, placed on that zone's main city. Your internet address is never looked up to find your location.
  • Feedback you send from the app: your note, what it's about, the rating if you gave one, and which screen you were on. Your email is shown with it only if you tick "You can email me about this".
  • When you agreed to the Terms, and when you confirmed a chat was one you were part of.
  • A daily count of how many AI replies your account used — just the number, not the messages.
  • Password reset links, if you use "Forgot password?": only a scrambled version is kept, and each link stops working after 30 minutes or once it's used.

You choose what imy learns from

  • imy never connects to your accounts. It doesn't link to Messenger, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Viber or any other app, and it will never ask for their passwords. It can't read your chats on its own. You download a chat yourself from the app and upload it, or upload screenshots, or paste text.
  • You pick the chats, and the parts of them. An uploaded chat is split into parts by date, and you untick anything you don't want imy to learn from. Later you can remove any message, any upload, or the whole person.
  • Private details are hidden before anything is saved. imy looks for passwords, one-time codes and PINs, card numbers, bank and e-wallet account numbers, government ID numbers, usernames, API keys, phone numbers and email addresses, and replaces each with a marker like [password hidden]. This covers everything you add: uploads, pasted text, edits, and what you type in a chat. What's hidden is never learned or repeated, and isn't sent to the AI service afterwards.
  • Screenshots are the exception. To read a screenshot, the picture itself is sent to Groq first, so Groq sees whatever it shows. The text imy keeps from it is then cleaned, but the picture is stored as you uploaded it. Review marks the screenshots that still show a hidden detail, so you can remove them. Crop or skip screenshots with passwords or account numbers in them.

Hiding is automatic pattern matching, so it can miss something or hide a harmless word. Please check Review and remove anything else private before you start chatting.

Cookies and browser storage

imy only uses what it needs to work, so there is no cookie banner to click through.

  • Sign-in cookie (imy_session): keeps you signed in on this device for up to 30 days, or until you sign out. The site can't work without it.
  • Admin cookie (imy_admin): only for the people who run imy, when they open the admin page. You will never get one.
  • Your theme (light or dark) is saved in your browser's own storage, on your device. It is never sent to the server.

There are no advertising, tracking or analytics cookies, and nothing from other companies is loaded. To remove all of the above, sign out and clear this site's data in your browser.

Who can see it

Only you, from your account. Every person you set up belongs to that account, and no other account can open them, read their messages or load their photos — not through the website, and not by guessing the address of a file.

The people running imy have an admin page. It shows how many people use imy, and a list of accounts with each one's email address, when it joined, when it was last active, how many people it has set up and on how many days it was used — numbers only — and a map of the time zones people use imy from. It never shows the names of the people you set up, your messages, your screenshots or your photos. It also shows the feedback you choose to send.

Whoever runs imy can technically reach its server, database, file storage and backups, as with any website. Your data is not sold and not used for advertising. imy runs on a few outside services, each holding only what its job needs:

  • Groq (the AI, see below): the messages and pictures sent to it for a reply, a photo description or reading a screenshot.
  • Turso (the database): your account, the people you set up, and every message.
  • Supabase (file storage): screenshots, profile pictures and photos you share. The storage is private; pictures are only shown through imy, and only to your account.
  • Resend (email): your email address and the emails imy sends you, like password-reset links.

These services may store or process data outside the Philippines.

The AI that writes the replies

Replies are written by an outside AI service, Groq, in the person's style. If Groq is busy or unavailable, imy writes the reply itself from patterns in the messages you uploaded. What gets sent is only what's needed for that one job:

  • a description of how the person writes, and a sample of their real messages;
  • the last few messages of your conversation;
  • a photo you share in a chat, so the reply can be about the photo;
  • a screenshot you upload, so Groq can read the messages in it. The picture is then kept in imy's own file storage, not by Groq.

Your email address and your password are never sent, and nor are the private details hidden from your chats, except inside a screenshot's picture (see above). Groq says that by default it doesn't keep what's sent to it; it may keep it for up to 30 days to investigate errors or abuse unless that's switched off, and it processes it in the United States (Groq: your data).

Each account can use the AI a set number of times a day. After that, replies are written by imy itself from the messages you uploaded, without sending anything out.

You can switch the outside AI off for your whole account at any time: account menu → turn off "Let an outside AI help write replies". After that nothing you write or share is sent out. Replies are written by imy itself from the messages you uploaded, photos you share are no longer described, and screenshots can't be read (upload the chat file or paste the text instead). The switch is on by default, which is why the Terms and this page ask you to agree when you sign up.

Deleting things

  • One person: open their chat, then the menu → Delete. Their messages, screenshots and shared photos go with them.
  • One conversation: the chat menu → Clear chat.
  • What they remember: the chat menu → What they remember → Forget everything.
  • Everything: your account menu → Delete everything. This removes your account, every person, every message, every uploaded file, your feedback and your activity dates from imy's database and file storage. It cannot be undone.

Deleted means deleted — not hidden. Backups made before a deletion, and the database host's own short restore history, may still hold the data until they age out, which takes about a week.

The person you're copying

This matters more than anything else on this page. imy learns from conversations involving a real person who isn't here to agree to it.

  • Only upload chats you were actually part of.
  • Don't use imy to impersonate someone to other people, or to pass its replies off as really theirs.
  • imy writes in someone's style. It is not them, it doesn't know what they'd really say, and it should never be treated as their words.
  • If you are the person someone has copied and you want that removed, get in touch below and it will be deleted.

Age

imy is for people aged 18 and over, which you confirm when you make an account. The AI services it relies on set that limit in their own terms.

Looking after yourself

imy can be a kind thing — a way to keep a voice close when someone is far away. It can also make a loss harder to sit with. If talking to it starts to hurt more than it helps, that's a good reason to step away for a while, and to talk to someone you trust. In the Philippines, the National Center for Mental Health crisis line is 1553, free from landlines and most mobile networks.

Your rights

Under the Philippines' Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act 10173), and similar laws elsewhere such as the GDPR for people in Europe and the UK, you can:

  • get a copy of what imy holds about you: account menu → Download my data, a zip with your chats, answers, notes and files;
  • have wrong information corrected;
  • have your data deleted. You can do this yourself at any time (see "Deleting things"), or ask us;
  • object to how your data is used. You can stop it going to the AI service yourself: account menu → turn off "Let an outside AI help write replies". For anything else, write to us;
  • take back your agreement at any time. Deleting your account does this.

Write to the address below and we'll answer within 30 days. If you think your data has been handled badly and we haven't put it right, you can complain to the Philippines' National Privacy Commission (privacy.gov.ph) or to your local data protection authority.
